# Use Claude Projects to Keep Reference Files for One Ongoing Task

> **In short:** Claude Projects lets you keep documents and standing instructions in one place, so every chat inside that project starts with the same background. Anthropic's help center says Projects are open to free accounts, with a limit of five projects on the free plan.

If you keep returning to the same task, such as a monthly report, a class project or a recurring client email, you have probably pasted the same background into Claude again and again. This guide shows you how to create a Claude Project, add your reference files, and write a short set of instructions so each new chat begins from the same starting point. You will need some experience with Claude already.

## Before you start

- A Claude account (free or paid) and access to Claude on the web or in the desktop or mobile app. You should already know how to start a chat and send a message.
- Two or three documents you return to often, such as a style guide, a template or meeting notes. Plain text, Word or PDF files work well.
- About 20 minutes for the full setup.

## Step 1 — Create a new project

Hover over the left side of your Claude screen and click **Projects**. If you don't see that word, look for a folder-style icon or a section labeled with projects in the left panel. You can also go straight to claude.ai/projects in your browser. Click **+ New Project** in the upper-right corner. Give it a short name that describes the ongoing task, such as "Monthly sales report." Add a description if you like. Anthropic's help center notes that Claude will not have access to this name and description, so they are only for your own organization. If you're on a Team or Enterprise plan, you may also see visibility settings; choose "Keep it private" unless you intend to share.

💬 Example: name the project "[task name]" and describe it as "[one-sentence description of the task]."

If it looks different: the button may appear as a plus sign or "New project" depending on your screen size. On a phone, open the menu first.

You'll know it worked when your new project opens and you can see an area for its knowledge and instructions.

## Step 2 — Add your reference documents to project knowledge

Open your project. The project knowledge area is on the right side of the project's main page. Click the **+** button to add content. You can upload documents, text files or code snippets. Anything you add here is used across all chats inside this project, so you won't need to paste it again.

Choose the two or three files that a new chat would need to do the work well. Adding everything you own can make the material harder to use, not easier. If you're on a paid plan and your material grows close to Claude's context window (the amount of text it can keep in view at once), Claude can automatically switch to a retrieval mode to handle more. Free plans don't have that automatic expansion, so keep the files focused.

💬 Example: upload your style guide, your monthly report template and last month's summary.

If it looks different: on a phone, the upload option may sit behind a plus icon inside the project screen.

You'll know it worked when your uploaded files appear in the project's knowledge list.

## Step 3 — Write project instructions

Still inside the project, find the option to **Set project instructions** and click it. In the box, describe how you want Claude to behave for this task: the audience, the tone, the length and the format you want. Keep it short, around one paragraph or a short bulleted list. Then click **Save instructions**. Claude uses these instructions in every chat within the project.

Good instructions say what the output is for and what to avoid. Vague wording such as "be helpful" adds little. Specific wording such as "write for a non-technical manager and keep each summary under 150 words" gives Claude something to follow.

💬 Example: "Write for [audience] in a [tone] tone. Keep each reply under [number] words and use short bullet points for lists."

If it looks different: the instructions box may open in a side panel or a pop-up. The wording of the button may vary slightly.

You'll know it worked when your instructions appear saved on the project page.

## Step 4 — Start a chat inside the project and test it

Click the option to start a new chat from within the project, so the chat belongs to it. Type a request for your ongoing task without restating the background. For example, you don't need to paste your style guide again.

Check whether the answer follows your files and instructions. If it misses the point, add more detail to your request in the same chat, then compare the result with your original material. Claude can make mistakes, so check figures, names and dates against your own documents before you use the answer. Claude can't see anything outside the project's knowledge and your chat unless you add it, so it may not know about last week's changes unless you tell it.

💬 Example: "Draft this month's summary using the sales figures I've shared, following the style guide."

If it looks different: if you don't see a way to start a chat from inside the project, open the project and look for a new chat option on its main page.

You'll know it worked when the reply reflects your instructions and the material from your files.

## Step 5 — Move an existing chat into the project

If you already have a useful chat about this task, you can move it into the project. Find the chat in your chat list, click the dropdown arrow next to its name, and choose **Add to project**. Pick the project from the window that opens and click it to move the chat in. You can also use the same dropdown inside a chat to remove it from a project or move it to another one.

Each project has its own memory, which means Claude remembers details from chats in that project. Memory from other projects isn't used there. If you want to keep a project's memory fully separate, turn off **Use account memory** under the Memory setting on the project's page. Anthropic's help center describes this behavior, so check the current settings if your screen looks different.

💬 Example: move the chat called "[old chat name]" into the project so future work can build on it.

If it looks different: the dropdown may appear as a three-dot menu on a phone or in a different corner of the chat list.

You'll know it worked when the chat appears inside your project.

## Common mistakes

- **Uploading too much.** A pile of unrelated files makes the project harder to use. Fix it by keeping only the two or three documents you use most often, and replacing them when they change.
- **Assuming context carries across every chat.** Anthropic's help center notes that context is not shared across chats unless the information is in the project knowledge base. Fix it by adding anything every chat needs to the knowledge area.
- **Expecting Claude to be an authority.** Claude can help you organize and draft, but it can make errors and doesn't know about changes you haven't shared. Fix it by checking important figures and facts against your original documents.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Set up one project for a recurring household or hobby task, such as planning a monthly budget review or a weekly meal plan, and keep your notes in one place.
- **For your business or work:** Create a project for a recurring report, client update or training material. Add your template and style guide once, so each new draft follows the same format.
- **If you want to go further:** Organize several projects by task and use the star option to keep your most-used ones near the top of your list. You can also review and refine your instructions after each round of drafts to tighten the results over time.

## Try it now

Create one project today, name it after a task you repeat, and upload one document you always find yourself re-explaining. Then type one request in a new chat inside that project and see whether the reply already reflects your material.
